decisions.sheet: Prompt 1 calls the overshirt "slate"; the drawing renders it #37383F, lighter than the near-black tee.
decisions.chosen: Overshirt #37383F with one shadow tone (recorded in palette.ts).
decisions.why: The approved drawing defines garments; brand slate stays for props.

decisions.sheet: The beard is drawn lighter and warmer than the hair (medians #845D40 chin, #77563F cheek vs hair #594235); palette v1 had beard = hair.
decisions.chosen: beard #7A5940, beardShadow #5E4535 (palette.ts, ZOO keys only).
decisions.why: Front and expression panels agree; matching them keeps the face recognisable.

decisions.sheet: In the front turnaround the face sits ~5 u right of the body axis (eye centre +5.5, jaw centre +1.5).
decisions.chosen: Face centred on the body axis; the hair keeps its measured asymmetry relative to the face (from zoo_expr_neutral.png).
decisions.why: The offset is inconsistent within the drawing itself (drawing jitter); the hair-to-face relationship is the identity-bearing feature.

decisions.sheet: The front turnaround places brows, eyes, nose and moustache ~3 u lower than the neutral close-up (same hair top and chin).
decisions.chosen: Front-view heights: eye line -816.5, moustache top -782.6, mouth line -768.3; shapes taken from the close-ups.
decisions.why: Reference priority: front and turnaround views control anatomy; expression drawings show performance.

decisions.sheet: The front turnaround shows level brows; the Neutral (deadpan) panel shows the anatomical-left brow ~3 u higher with an arch.
decisions.chosen: Neutral keeps the subtly raised anatomical-left brow.
decisions.why: Prompt 1 defines neutral acting as "flat straight mouth and subtly raised brow"; browLift and the other expressions animate from there.

decisions.sheet: The mouth panels draw the lower face ~15% narrower than the turnaround.
decisions.chosen: Face width from the turnaround; mouth shapes matched in size and placement relative to the moustache.
decisions.why: Reference priority (front view controls anatomy).

decisions.sheet: The Shocked panel shows a medium open oval mouth (about 17 x 11 u), between "oh" and "ah".
decisions.chosen: Shocked defaults to the "ah" library shape at 70% opening and 82% width instead of adding a seventh shape.
decisions.why: Keeps the fixed six-shape mouth library while matching the panel.

decisions.sheet: The pointing panel draws the shoulders ~35 u higher than the turnaround; its upper arm is ~30 deg from vertical.
decisions.chosen: Superseded by ZOO-P2 (repair round 1). v1: upper arm 46 deg, forearm ~50 deg, index ~15 deg up, tip at h ~691.
decisions.why: Matching the panel angles on the turnaround body left the hand at chest height; Prompt 2 and the panel both put the point at shoulder height.

decisions.sheet: In the front view each sleeve's inner contour coincides with the overshirt side contour.
decisions.chosen: Arms are layered behind the overshirt panels.
decisions.why: Identical at rest, and a raised arm emerges from under the shoulder seam instead of cutting a line across the chest.

decisions.sheet: Ears, eyes, hands, sleeves, legs, shoes and collar leaves are drawn as symmetric pairs; hair, brow raise, smirk, buttons, pocket and pin are one-sided.
decisions.chosen: Unmarked pairs are authored once and mirrored to the other side inside the same view; one-sided items are drawn per side and never mirrored.
decisions.why: Project rule: never flip an asymmetric character or its markings to make another view.

decisions.sheet: In the 3/4 turnaround the forelock tip sits almost on the facial midline (x~31, between the brows); in the front it hangs ~17 u to the anatomical right of the midline. Both drawings put it on the anatomical-right side of the crown hollow.
decisions.chosen: The 3/4 hair follows the 3/4 sheet: forelock tip at (31,-841), crown hollow to its anatomical left (screen right), wings at the back of the head. The profile puts the forelock in front of the forehead; from behind the big wings are on the anatomical right (screen right).
decisions.why: Turnaround views control identity; the hair-feature order agrees in every view and nothing is mirrored.

decisions.sheet: The 3/4 turnaround draws the mouth and moustache nearly symmetric about x~29 at ~0.86 of the front width, while the near (anatomical right) cheek beard extends about 2x further toward the ear.
decisions.chosen: One piecewise map tqX (views/threeQuarter/tq.ts): linear x0.86 inside the moustache tips, x2.0 on the near cheek, x0.25 on the far cheek. The front beard, moustache, smirk and the whole mouth library are drawn through it.
decisions.why: Keeps a single mouth library anchored consistently to the face in both views; fits the 3/4 drawing within ~2 u at the beard edge, lip patch and moustache tips.

decisions.sheet: Re-measured in repair round 1: the front turnaround puts the buttons at -672/-622/-565/-508/-452, the same top-button height as the 3/4 (-673). (v1 recorded -686 for the front, which was a mis-measure.)
decisions.chosen: Buttons at -672/-622/-565/-508/-452 in every view (front, 3/4, side, typing via the 3/4 torso).
decisions.why: Same garment in every view; front controls anatomy and costume, and the two drawings agree.

decisions.sheet: The 3/4 and profile turnaround brows are drawn ~4-5 u thick; the front rig brows are ~8 u thick (matched to the front close-ups).
decisions.chosen: The 3/4 and profile brows reuse the front brow shapes and expression poses, thinned about their mid-line (x0.7 in 3/4, x0.8 in profile).
decisions.why: Keeps the brow design and expression behaviour identical while matching the turned views of the sheet.

decisions.sheet: The side view shows the back of the near hand with four separate fingers and no separate thumb; the 3/4 and back hands are the front relaxed hand seen from those angles (row scans: 3/4 near ~47 u wide, far ~27 u, back ~31 u).
decisions.chosen: Repair round 2 (supersedes round 1's point-mapped front palm drawing, which showed the front thumb hook from behind and in 3/4): every view draws its own hand with HandDrawing (parts/Hand.tsx): front = palm-side relaxed hand with an open thumb gap; back = the back of the hand with four tip lobes stepping toward the thigh and the thumb tucked out of view; 3/4 near = the back of the hand with four stepped fingertips and a shorter thumb lobe; 3/4 far = little-finger side with the fingers curled toward the body; profile = four fingers parting from y -366 (~36% of the hand; round 1 ~24%). One silhouette each with a centred near-black outline on the silhouette only and thin warm-brown separations. Pairs are mirrored only inside one view.
decisions.why: Front and turnaround views control anatomy; at the asset sheet's lineScale (1.59) round 1's full-weight thumb hook and 18-24 u near-black finger lines read as black talons.

decisions.sheet: The pin shows on the far chest in 3/4 and is not drawn in the profile or back views. The far arm and far leg are hidden in the profile.
decisions.chosen: Same: pin on the far (anatomical left) panel in 3/4, hidden in side/back; profile draws only the near arm and near leg.
decisions.why: Anatomical placement: the anatomical-left chest faces away from the camera in both views.

decisions.sheet: The typing panel draws the head ~25% larger relative to the body than the turnaround (the point panel shows the same drift).
decisions.chosen: The typing pose uses the turnaround proportions (head 160 u). For comparison the panel is framed at 1.555 u/px, which makes its head 168 u and lines up desk, chair, knees and feet.
decisions.why: Reference priority: turnaround controls anatomy; pose drawings show performance.

decisions.sheet: Seated, the panel hides the overshirt hem behind the desk edge; the standing 3/4 torso would put the hem ~50 u over the thighs.
decisions.chosen: The seated torso is the 3/4 torso scaled x0.88 vertically about its shoulder line, so the hem rests on the lap; pin, pocket and top buttons move by < 4 u.
decisions.why: Reads as the shirt bunching when he sits; keeps every costume detail in place.

decisions.sheet: The panel draws a light-grey desk, a mid-grey office chair, a dark-grey monitor and a near-black keyboard; palette v1 had no prop colours.
decisions.chosen: PROP_COLORS in palette.ts (sampled; one shadow tone each, desk = brand silver).
decisions.why: Props must share the flat style without ad-hoc hex values.

decisions.sheet: The panel draws the forearms ~45% longer than the turnaround (elbow at the back of the torso, hands far forward on the keyboard).
decisions.chosen: Turnaround forearm length (~115 u elbow to cuff end) with the elbow under the shoulder; the keyboard sits nearer to him (TYPING_LAYOUT.keyboard). The far forearm emerges from behind the torso.
decisions.why: Reference priority (anatomy from the turnaround); the pose still reads as the panel: seated upright, forearms forward, both hands on the keys.

decisions.sheet: The only typing drawing is a 3/4 view facing screen right.
decisions.chosen: pose="typing" always draws that 3/4 pose; the view prop is ignored for it.
decisions.why: No reference exists for other typing angles; inventing one would risk drift.

decisions.sheet: zoo_expr_neutral.png (contrast-enhanced) and zoo_turn_front.png: the forelock is a curved horn out of the middle lock with its tip at (-17,-842); a near-black arch-shaped hollow (median #2A201A) sits under the rolling top lock; the sides end at the ear tops.

decisions.why: Front and bust drawings agree within ~4 u; the hollow is an ink accent, not a third hair tone (one shadow tone per colour).

decisions.sheet: The shocked and worried panels raise the brows 6-13 u while both brows stay fully visible below the forelock tip.
decisions.chosen: Brows draw after the front hair in every view; when a raised brow would come within 1.6 u of the forelock tip, the forelock lower part lifts by the difference (forelockLiftFor in parts/Hair.tsx; FORELOCK34_TIP in the 3/4 head).

decisions.sheet: Prompt 1 defines the deadpan as a "subtly raised brow" (one brow); the sheet raises the anatomical-left brow.
decisions.chosen: browLift 0..1 raises the anatomical-left brow 4.5 u and the right 1.6 u (v1 raised both 3.5 u).
decisions.why: A one-sided raise reads as unimpressed rather than surprised.

decisions.sheet: Pixel medians: moustache #634732/#684A33 (darker than chin #845D40); hair #584033/#574134; irises #292422/#261F1C; brows #241F19; nose bridge #906C55; lip line core #5C3D2C.
decisions.chosen: palette.ts: moustache #664933 (flat, new key), hair #584134 (was #5E4637), eyeIris #2C221D (was #5A3E2B), brow #221C18 (was #3A2A20), noseLine #8E6A54 (new line colour for the nose bridge and ear fold); the closed lip line uses beardShadow.
decisions.why: Matches the approved sheet; all are ZOO-only keys and keep one shadow tone per colour (moustache and noseLine have none).

decisions.sheet: The sheet keeps a near-constant screen line weight (~3 u at full body, ~1.6 u at bust framing); interior face lines are thin and soft.
decisions.chosen: lines.ts ZOO_LINE (outline 3.5, detail 2.25, fine 1.4, lid 2.45, feature 1.62, all from LINE) replaces scattered literals; ZooRig lineScale multiplies every stroke and lineScaleFor(pxPerUnit) implements ART_GUIDE SL5. Lids and nostrils are tapered filled shapes; no outer-corner lash flick.
decisions.why: Close-ups no longer read as a thick-lined sticker; one line system for every view.

decisions.sheet: The mouth panels draw the lower face ~19% narrower; measured RELATIVE TO THE MOUSTACHE the library sizes match (oh 17 x 15.5 u vs 16.7 x 14.9; ah 28 x 19 vs 25 x 19.6). Lip lines and rims are thin and dark brown.
decisions.chosen: Mouth sizes kept (a review asked to shrink "oh" by 30% using absolute panel units, which ignores ZOO-M1); closed/mbp drawn as thin beardShadow lip lines (1.6 / 1.9 u), open rims 1.62 u; mouth line raised 1.3 u (jaw pivot -769.6) to the sheet gap under the moustache; moustache two-lobed with a philtrum notch and pointed tips.
decisions.why: ZOO-M1 anchors the mouth library to the moustache; the line styling follows every mouth panel.

decisions.sheet: zoo_expr_worried.png: inner brow ends rise 5-7.5 u with a sharp upturn, the screen-right arch inverts ~4 u, tails rise ~1.5-2 u. Shocked: brows ~8-11 u up, wide horizontal oval mouth. Happy: soft closed U-smile, lower lids up, head turned ~15 deg.
decisions.chosen: Brow pose gains `curl` (inner-end upturn); worried/happy/shocked presets re-measured (worried inner-to-tail drop >= 11 u; happy cornerL 3.2 / cornerR 6.4, lidBottom 2.4; shocked brows +7.6/+8.2 with arch 3, mouth ah x0.95 wide x0.6 open). The front head does NOT yaw for happy.
decisions.why: Restrained adult acting that reads at video scale; a yaw on the front head would slide features over a static skull, so the turned-head happy is left to view="threeQuarter" (known gap). Repair round 2: both corners lift more (cornerL 3.2 -> 4.5, moustacheLiftR 3.6 -> 4) so the smile reads at bust size without the turn.

decisions.sheet: zoo_pose_point.png: upper arm ~42 deg out from vertical, forearm rising ~52 deg, index ~25 deg up and ~45 u above the shoulder; the sleeve flows out of the shoulder; the relaxed hand never shows as a flat open hand.
decisions.chosen: SUPERSEDED by ZOO-P4 (repair round 2); the shoulder follow and the rounded elbow disk remain. Round 1: end key shoulder -44 / elbow -93 / wrist 22 (upper arm 43 deg, forearm 57 deg, index ~22 deg up, tip h ~720 on the turnaround body); in-between -20/-92/5 (hand lifts in front of the chest, 38 deg wrist drag); loose fist 0.08..0.4, pointer from 0.4; the overshirt shoulder follows the arm; rounded elbow disk; head/eye bias toward the point unless animated by the caller. Clearance re-checked on the joint chain and in proof frames f93-f96 / f186-f192: the hand stays >= 18 u from Badger's head at the proof spacing (560 u).
decisions.why: Fixes the low hand, the shoulder notch, the limp chicken-wing in-between and the hand pop while keeping INT-P2 staging valid.

decisions.sheet: zoo_pose_point.png traced on a world grid: an OPEN elbow (~95 deg inside), forearm rising ~42 deg, index ~3 deg above horizontal with its tip at (358, h733), ~55 u above the cuff because the index rides on top of an upright fist (thumb and three curled fingers stacked under it); sleeves ~40-42 u wide.
decisions.chosen: End key shoulder -44 / elbow -93 / wrist 22: upper arm 49 deg from vertical, forearm rising 48 deg, elbow ~91 deg inside, index ~6-7 deg up, fingertip (378, h719). Pointer redrawn from the panel (upright fist, 0.92 x panel size = 13% larger than round 1). Mid key -20/-92/5 (upper arm abducted, elbow outside the overshirt, forearm 23 deg up, straight wrist). Joints follow monotone cubics through the keys with POINT_OVERLAP (elbow leads, shoulder lags and first tucks the elbow 6 deg); loose fist from 0.08, pointer from 0.4. Proof check (Preview10s at 560 u spacing, rendered): hand path monotonic out and up, elbow x >= 101 throughout, closest approach to Badger's head 30.5 u (27 px) at f96 (an outward path without the tuck came within 6 u).
decisions.why: Fixes the acute V, the 26-deg upward jab, the thin sleeve and the waist-level chicken wing. The turnaround arm is longer than the panel's, so the panel's own angles put the fingertip ~30 u too low; the upper arm is raised 6 deg more than the panel's (49 vs ~43) to keep the tip at the round-1 height (h ~719 vs the panel's 733). Turnaround controls anatomy; the pose panel shows performance.

decisions.why: Turnaround controls anatomy; pose panels show performance. Revisit with a proper leg rig.

decisions.sheet: Row scans of zoo_turn_front.png: cuff centre ~4 u further in than v1, sleeve outer edge 2.5-4 u in; the relaxed hand tapers and curls toward the thigh with a separate thumb lobe; sneakers narrow at the ankle with a convex toe box; trouser hem drapes over the tongue.
decisions.chosen: Forearm/cuff and wrist pivots moved in 2.2 u, upper-arm outer edge in 2.5-4 u; relaxed hand redrawn (PALM/THUMB/FINGER_LINES); shoes reshaped (outer edge ~82 at the ankle to ~109 at the sole), three lace bars, terminator shadow; hem lowered to a break at -44.6.
decisions.why: Front view controls anatomy; v1 hands read as paddles and the shoes as boats.

decisions.sheet: zoo_pose_typing.png: two full-size hands side by side over a ~185 u keyboard; the monitor seen from behind (plain back panel, lit left edge, neck in front, flat foot); he leans toward the screen.
decisions.chosen: Typing hands x1.36/1.3 at wrists (-101,-384) / (-19,-387), near hand over the far cuff; keyboard 186 u at x 20; monitor redrawn from behind; upper body offset +6/+10 toward the screen and down with the near shoulder following (eyes within ~4 u of the panel); default look/tilt toward the screen (TYPING_LOOK).
decisions.why: Fixes the undersized claw hands and the screen-out monitor while keeping the turnaround proportions (ZOO-T1, ZOO-T4).

decisions.sheet: zoo_turn_34.png / zoo_turn_side.png / zoo_turn_back.png: 3/4 nose bridge x 36 -> 44 with the nostril at ~33; 3/4 forelock a rounded lock end at (32,-840); profile forelock a C-curl hanging to (72,-839) with ~7 u of nasal bridge in front of the eye; back crown one S-shaped lock; wave strands are curved and brown.
decisions.chosen: Repair round 1: 3/4 nose +8 u with the front nose construction; 3/4 forelock rounded and liftable; profile eye moved back 3 u (front corner 5 u), nasal bridge 2-3 u forward, C-curl forelock; profile mouth interior ends at the lip fronts with a thin lip line; back crown S-curve; long crown seams replaced by short curved hair-shadow strands in every view; one ear fold line in the nose-line brown.
decisions.why: Turnaround views control identity; each change was measured on its own panel.

decisions.sheet: zoo_turn_front.png row scan at the same world scale: below the chest the overshirt narrows to +-87..89 and the sleeves (46-48 u, cuff ~39 u) hang free with 4-7 u of background between each cuff and the hem from y -480; hem 172-178 u.
decisions.chosen: Repair round 2: each front panel follows the shoulder line to the shoulder point, turns down an armhole seam and runs down the body side at +-86..89; sleeves widened (inner edge ~94, cuff 97.8..129.4); elbow pivots +-111.5 (sleeve centre), wrist pivots +-113.8 (cuff centre); panel shadow kept to a ~5 u band inside the side edge. Measured: sides +-87..88, gap 4-7 u, hem 172 u, cuff 39 u.
decisions.why: Front view controls anatomy; round 1 kept the panels at +-101..103 to the hem and hid ~13 u of each sleeve, so Zoo read stockier than the lean sheet figure.

decisions.sheet: zoo_expr_neutral.png teal rows at 0.699 u/px: dome ~17.5 x 11.2 u; three tentacles ~9.8 u long inside the dome width (~14 u spread), each cased in near-black.
decisions.chosen: Repair round 2: dome half-width 7.8, tentacles end at +8.2 (x1 within +-5.2), near-black casing under each teal tentacle, teal width and casing both scaled by lineScale (PIN_SHAPE in parts/Pin.tsx); size 1.15, centre (58,-660).
decisions.why: Locked design: "one tiny teal jellyfish pin: small dome with three short tentacles"; round 1's 15 u splayed legs read as a squid.

decisions.sheet: Front busts and zoo_turn_front.png: each ear is a rounded C whose lobe tucks into the face at ~-785.
decisions.chosen: Repair round 2: the ear spline closes INSIDE the face edge (lobe ... (41,-782.4), (38.2,-786), (37.6,-792)), so no pointed lobe hangs over the jaw line.
decisions.why: Round 1 ended the closed spline outside the face and drew an elf tip.

decisions.sheet: zoo_turn_back.png: the crown carries a dark S-shaped lock plus the top-lock and left-lock edges; the nape is shaded under wavy lock ends.
decisions.chosen: Repair round 2: the S-lock, top-lock and left-lock edges are tapered ink lines in ZOO_COLORS.brow (the hair ink already used for the front crown hollow), up to ZOO_LINE.detail wide, clipped to the hair; one hair-shadow region = a thin crescent under the S-lock and the nape below a wavy edge; the isolated groove oval is gone.
decisions.why: From behind, the S-lock is the hair's identity; round 1's strands in the shadow tone were invisible and the flat lower band read as a two-tone helmet.

decisions.sheet: zoo_pose_typing.png: two soft hands whose fingers arc down and forward onto the keys with thin separations; the monitor back is a plain panel with square corners.
decisions.chosen: Repair round 2: each typing hand is ONE silhouette (back of the hand + four tip lobes landing 5-8 u ahead of the knuckle line on the keys, thumb in skin) with thin warm-brown separations along the finger arcs; taps move the tip lobes. The monitor panel and foot are straight-edged polygons with small fillets (path extent = its corners, y -275.4..-71.6). Chair wheel and leg outlines follow lineScale.
decisions.why: Round 1's separately outlined hooked fingers stacked into black knots; the monitor spline overshot 11.4 u past each corner.

decisions.sheet: The sheet's close-up nostrils are ~1.7 u dark commas and the bust lid lines stay heavy, while outlines thin to ~1.6 u.
decisions.chosen: featureScale(ls, min) in lines.ts: the nose bridge and nostrils keep their drawn size below lineScale 1 (and thicken above it); the upper-lid line floors at 0.85. Applied in the front, 3/4 and profile heads.
decisions.why: Facial feature shapes are part of the face design, not outlines; at ls ~0.5 round 1 shrank the nostrils to ~0.9 u hairlines.

decisions.sheet: The expression and mouth panels draw the torso ~6 u higher than the turnaround: 28.7 u of neck and the pin centroid at ~-669.8 against the turnaround's 34.3 u and -659.4.
decisions.chosen: The turnaround neck, collar, tee and pin heights are used in every framing; the bust panels are performance references for the face only.
decisions.why: Reference priority: front and turnaround views control anatomy; recorded so reviews do not re-flag the busts as long-necked.

decisions.sheet: zoo_expr_neutral.png, zoo_turn_side.png, zoo_turn_34.png: shallow philtrum dip (moustache ~9.5 u thick at x=0); forelock ~12 u wide at y -850; profile eye a mostly dark almond (~25-30% white); profile moustache merging into the cheek beard; throat skin right under the 3/4 jaw; only a soft shadow tight under the jaw.
decisions.chosen: Repair round 2: moustache notch at -784 with a 0.6 u dip; forelock 11.6 u at -850 (concave right edge ~2.5 u further right, left edge ~1 u left, tip unchanged); profile eye back corner -4.5, iris rx 0.8r, highlight 0.6x; profile moustache ends blunt ~2 u inside the beard; 3/4 throat top tucked 0.5-1.5 u above the jaw line; jaw shadows in front, 3/4, typing and profile reduced to <= 6 u crescents under the jaw.
decisions.why: Each change measured on its own panel; turnaround views control identity.

decisions.sheet: zoo_turn_side.png / zoo_turn_34.png / zoo_turn_front.png: chunky low-tops whose toe box keeps its height (~31 u) to a round nose; the 3/4 near toe reaches x ~-22 over the far heel; front shoes flare slightly on the inner side too; ~55 u of shoe shows below the front hem.
decisions.chosen: Repair round 2: side and 3/4-far toe boxes hold their top to ~8 u from the tip, then round down; 3/4 near shoe extended to a round toe at x ~-22; front inner edge flares from ~30 (y -40) to ~25 at the sole; front hem break raised 8 u (-44.6 -> -52.6), ~52 u of shoe shows.
decisions.why: Round 1 tapered the toes into pointed slippers, cut the near 3/4 shoe into a clog and showed too little shoe in front.

decisions.sheet: zoo_turn_front.png: the relaxed thumb joins the back of the hand at the top; the thumb/index notch starts about 40% down the hand, and the finger separations run about a third of the hand length.
decisions.chosen: Integration fix (2026-11-24): the thumb is filled without a full outline; only the tip and the lower notch are stroked (THUMB_EDGE). Finger separation lines lengthened from 7 to about 18 units.
decisions.why: The full thumb outline ran up to the cuff and read as a separate hook in the 10 s proof; front view controls anatomy.

decisions.sheet: zoo_turn_front.png: the tee ends at the overshirt hem; no tee tail shows over the trousers.
decisions.chosen: Integration fix: the tee's two hem key points are corners, so the closed Catmull-Rom spline no longer overshoots ~30 units below the hem.
decisions.why: The rounded tee tail was a spline artefact, not part of the design.

decisions.sheet: zoo_pose_point.png shows only the end pose; the size-comparison panel puts Badger just beside ZOO's hand.
decisions.chosen: The point blend follows a quadratic joint-space arc through ARM_POINT_MID (elbow in, forearm lifts with the hand trailing, then the upper arm opens and the hand follows through). Revised in repair round 1 as ZOO-P2 (new end key, 38 deg wrist drag instead of 75, loose-fist transition, pointer from 0.5).
decisions.why: The old blend swung the hand through the head of a dog standing beside him (checked on the joint chain: it needed Badger 656 units away; this path clears him from 554). Overlapping action and follow-through also read as a more natural, restrained gesture.

decisions.sheet: Size panel: withers 312.6, head top 451.9, ear top 455.6, body length 348 units (body:withers 1.11). The left coat map draws a longer body (1.23 at the same withers height).
decisions.chosen: Size-panel numbers are binding. The coat-map trace is mapped with ky 1.0455 / kx 0.9398 so withers and body length hit the panel exactly.
decisions.why: Reference priority: the size-comparison panel controls relative scale. The coat map still controls where every marking sits on each part.

decisions.sheet: Coat map: far front leg hidden behind the near leg. Size panel: both far legs placed forward and visible.
decisions.chosen: view 'left' stand uses the size-panel stance: far front leg 38 sheet px forward of the near leg, far hind leg 33 px forward, both in coatShadow.
decisions.why: The standing view is the one shown next to ZOO and must match that panel. The stance does not change any marking (leg spots ride on their segments).

decisions.sheet: badger_coat_top.png draws the dark ear on the side that is the dog’s anatomical RIGHT in a top view.
decisions.chosen: The dark cap is on the anatomical LEFT ear in every view.
decisions.why: Reference priority: the front head controls which ear is dark (dark ear on viewer’s right in the front view).

decisions.sheet: badger_coat_left.png draws the large withers patch on the left side; badger_coat_right.png draws only a thickened top line at the withers; badger_coat_top.png draws the patch straddling the spine (its front half reaches 0.84 of the half-width on the right and 0.86 on the left); the turnaround side, 3/4, walking, looking-up, sitting and lying panels (all right-facing) draw it large on the visible side.
decisions.chosen: One marking, L-WITHERS: high on the back at the LEFT withers, its front half wrapping over the spine onto the right side. From the left it is the full patch (coat_left); from the right it is that right lobe (D16); from behind it is the crescent under the collar (D20).
decisions.why: The three labelled coat maps control body markings and agree only if the patch straddles the spine; PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS place it near the LEFT withers.

decisions.sheet: Front/expression heads show one cheek spot on each side; every profile drawing (coat maps, turnaround side, looking-up) shows none.
decisions.chosen: H-CHEEK-L / H-CHEEK-R are drawn in front and 3/4 heads and hidden in profile and look-up heads.
decisions.why: The front head controls facial markings and these spots sit on the front plane of the cheek beside the muzzle; the profiles on the sheet consistently omit them.

decisions.sheet: Coat map shows a spot on the near forearm; the small size panel omits it.
decisions.chosen: Spot L-09 is kept on legFrontNear.upper.
decisions.why: Coat maps control body markings; the size panel only controls scale.

decisions.sheet: In the size panel the body faces left and the face is turned to camera with only a slight lean to screen left.
decisions.chosen: Default head for view 'left' is 'front' (threeQuarterLeftScreen is a true 3/4).
decisions.why: Measured: the panel nose sits ~16 units left of the skull centre, far closer to the front head than to the turnaround 3/4 (nose at the far contour).

decisions.sheet: Only one 3/4 head (facing screen right) on the turnaround.
decisions.chosen: Both 3/4 heads are built from the front head by a depth-field turn of 36 deg calibrated to badger_turn_34.png proportions (near eye 0.43, nose 0.88 of head width). Each ear keeps its own front-view shape, colour and marking; the far ear goes behind the skull.
decisions.why: Gives symmetric, consistent 3/4 angles without horizontally flipping any asymmetric marking.

decisions.sheet: badger_coat_right.png: right profile with the pale right ear (a rose flap with a small dark spot) as the near ear; badger_turn_side.png shows the ear's pink inner at the fold.
decisions.chosen: REVISED in round-1 repair and corrected in round 2: profileRightScreen's skull outline, stop, nose, muzzle underside and the pale ear (outline, fold line, pink band at the fold from turn_side, spot H-EAR-R-SPOT) are traced on coat_right; its eye, brow and the four expression mouth paths are the left profile's, mirrored about the head and re-fitted to coat_right (these are unmarked, symmetric features; nothing marked is mirrored). v1.0.0 mirrored the whole left profile, ear included; that is removed. Look-up heads are the profiles pitched 40 deg and joined to the rig necks (D27, D39).
decisions.why: Opposite views carry their own drawing and markings; the reviewers measured the old right ear as an exact mirror of the left one. The round-2 review found the round-1 text overstated what was retraced; this wording is what gen_heads.py does.

decisions.sheet: The pale ear flap is drawn in the same white as the head; its inner surface is pinkish grey.
decisions.chosen: Flap uses coat; inner uses earPaleInner. Palette key earPale (#E9E4E0) is left unused.
decisions.why: A second near-white would read as a dirty patch and act as a second shadow tone of the coat (one-shadow-tone rule).

decisions.sheet: Neutral face: soft grey brows. Happy/worried/shocked: thin near-black brows.
decisions.chosen: Added BADGER_COLORS.brow '#8E9299' for the soft brow; expressive and 'judge' brows add a near-black line (LINE.color).
decisions.why: Matches the sheet; brow is a line colour, not a shadow tone.

decisions.sheet: The sheet uses a constant pixel line width, so its enlarged expression heads have relatively thinner lines.
decisions.chosen: REVISED in round-1 repair: the default stays one outline weight in world units (LINE.width 3.5, details LINE.detailWidth). The optional prop lineScale (default 1) multiplies every outline and detail width (legs, collar, tag, face lines included), the same contract as ZooRig lineScale (decision ZOO-L1); badgerLineScaleFor(pxPerUnit) gives the ART_GUIDE SL5 value (outline 3-6 px at output), e.g. 1.53 at 0.56 px/unit and 0.54 at 3.2 px/unit. In a two-shot pass the same value to both characters.
decisions.why: Consistent near-black outlines across shots and scales (PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS style rule); below 0.857 px/unit the fixed width fell under SL5 (the pose row at 0.56 drew 1.96 px outlines). The scale is explicit, not derived from `scale`, because the output px per unit also depends on the parent viewBox, and Zoo uses the same explicit prop.

decisions.sheet: One round teal tag; edge-on (oval) in side views.
decisions.chosen: One tag: round disc in the front bust, edge-on oval in the left view, hanging plumb from the collar ring.
decisions.why: Single tag per the locked design; orientation follows the view.

decisions.sheet: badger_coat_right.png: the right side with its own spot pattern (9 marks) and only a sliver of the left withers patch at the top line.
decisions.chosen: view 'right' is its own trace of coat_right (rigRight.ts, gen_right.py), mapped with kx 0.9734 / ky 1.0283 so withers (312.3) and body length match the binding size panel (D01). Its markings are separate records R-01..R-08 and R-NECK; the patch edge keeps the id L-WITHERS (side left). Near ear: the pale right ear (profileRightScreen head).
decisions.why: The labelled coat maps control body markings; opposite views carry their own anatomical markings and nothing is flipped.

decisions.sheet: badger_coat_right.png and badger_turn_side.png show ONE front leg (row scans give a single pair of edges from the elbow to the paw); the far hind paw stands about 26 px ahead of the near one.
decisions.chosen: REVISED in round-1 repair: the far (left) front leg stands exactly behind the near one and is hidden; the far hind leg mounts 26 px forward. The v1.0.0 text (far front paw 30 px ahead) misread the map; a forward offset showed a grey extra leg and doubled the near leg's front outline. The right-view root origin stays where v1.0.0 put it so existing shots do not shift.
decisions.why: Matches the coat map and the turnaround side.

decisions.sheet: Six of the seven right-facing drawings (turnaround side, 3/4, walking, looking-up, sitting, lying) draw the large patch on the visible right side; coat_right shows only its top-line edge; the top map shows the front of the patch straddling the spine.
decisions.chosen: REVISED in round 2 (2026-11-24): right-facing level views (right stand, right walk, right look-up) show the right lobe of L-WITHERS as badger_turn_side.png draws it: a rounded irregular lens about 82 x 38 units hanging from the top line, its front about 22 sheet px behind the collar, traced on turn_side and mapped into coat_right space by the collar's back edge on the top line (dev/trace/gen_right.py). The round-1 pointed wedge (a compromise no drawing shows) is removed. The 3/4, sit and lie bodies keep the dorsal patch traced from their own panels. Same id, side left, authored per view, never mirrored. OWNER CONFIRMATION STILL REQUESTED: the alternative is coat_right's thin top-line edge (v1.0.0).
decisions.why: The three labelled coat maps disagree here (coat_right: a thickened top line; coat_top: the front half of the patch straddles the spine and covers 0.84 of the right half-width, which a level side camera sees as a deep lobe). The turnaround, which controls identity and anatomy, breaks the tie, and the walking and looking-up panels agree with it: seven of the eight right-facing drawings show the lens. The reviewers rejected both coat_right's edge (round 1) and the wedge (round 2).

decisions.sheet: The turnaround draws all four views at one scale; its side-view withers stand 329 crop px above the ground line (y=484).
decisions.chosen: Front, back and 3/4 bodies are traced at 0.950 units per crop px (312.6 / 329), so their withers match the binding size panel. The replaceable heads keep their size: the turnaround front skull measures 97.9 units against 99.5 for the shared front head.
decisions.why: Size panel controls scale; the turnaround controls anatomy. One head size in every view avoids a head that changes size on a view switch.

decisions.sheet: badger_turn_front.png: dark ear on screen right; spots on both shoulders, both forearms, one on the midline chest under the tag; neck spots on both sides; only a narrow strip of a hind leg between the front legs.
decisions.chosen: view 'front' traces the turnaround body, neck, collar and tag; head 'front' is mounted on the sheet's face centroid. Markings reuse the coat-map ids as seen from the front (R-04 / L-03 shoulders, R-08 / L-09 forearms, R-NECK / L-NECK) plus M-CHEST.
decisions.why: Front views control anatomy and the front head controls which ear is dark.

decisions.sheet: A spot on the midline of the chest below the tag (front, 3/4 and sitting drawings). No coat map can show the chest midline.
decisions.chosen: Kept as M-CHEST (side midline) on the front, 3/4 and sit bodies; it never appears in side views.
decisions.why: The turnaround front controls anatomy where no coat map covers the area; the side maps are not contradicted.

decisions.sheet: badger_turn_back.png: dark ear on SCREEN LEFT; a domed crescent under the collar (about 85 x 23 units); two large ovals on the upper rump; a spot on the back of the left thigh; one spot above each hock. The top map shows more spots on the dorsal surface.
decisions.chosen: REVISED in round-1 repair: the back view shows exactly what the turnaround back shows, traced at its size: T-PATCH (= L-WITHERS) as the crescent, T-05 (= R-01) and T-08 (= L-02) as the two ovals (by height they are the croup spots, 254 / 256 units, not the mid-back pair at 283 / 290), plus L-07, L-08, R-07. The other top-map spots (T-01, T-02, T-03 = R-04, T-04 = R-02, T-06 = L-03, T-07 = L-01) lie on the receding dorsal surface and are hidden at eye level. No mark is smaller than 13 units.
decisions.why: The top coat map keeps the identities (sameAs); the turnaround controls what an eye-level camera behind the dog sees. The v1.0.0 projection shrank spots to specks below the outline width, which read as freckles.

decisions.sheet: badger_coat_top.png is a dorsal view with the head at screen left.
decisions.chosen: Image TOP = anatomical RIGHT (a dog facing screen left, seen from above, has its right side at the top). Seen from behind, anatomical right = screen right, so T- spots from the image top land on screen right of the back view.
decisions.why: Keeps every marking on its anatomical side; consistent with D03 (top-map ear colour read the same way).

decisions.sheet: badger_turn_34.png: right flank toward camera; the withers patch drawn large on top of the back; a spot behind it; R-05 / R-06 omitted.
decisions.chosen: REVISED in round-1 repair: L-WITHERS is the dorsal patch traced from the turnaround 3/4 (about 50 x 36 units on top of the withers; the elevated camera sees the surface where the patch straddles the spine, D16). R-02 moves just behind it (foreshortened). Other markings follow coat_right as before (R-01..R-08, R-NECK, L-09 far forearm, L-03 far shoulder, M-CHEST).
decisions.why: Coat maps control markings; the 3/4 drawing shows how much of the dorsal surface is visible.

decisions.sheet: The sitting, lying, walking and looking-up panels all face screen right. Episodes stage Badger to the right of Zoo facing left, so a sit or lie beat must be able to face left.
decisions.chosen: REVISED in round-1 repair: sit and lie exist in both facings. view right (or front/back/3/4) uses the traced right-facing bodies with right-side markings. view left uses the same UNMARKED silhouette mirrored about the root (outline, collar and tag are bilaterally symmetric, the same approach as the 3/4-left skull) carrying the LEFT coat map's own markings authored for it (L-WITHERS as the full patch, L-01..L-09, L-NECK, R-08 on the far forearm edge, M-CHEST) and head threeQuarterLeftScreen (dark ear near). walk and lookUp are built on both side rigs as before.
decisions.why: v1.0.0 silently rendered the right-facing body for view left, turning Badger away from Zoo and swapping his visible markings mid-scene. Only symmetric anatomy is reused; no marking is flipped. Round-2 note: the sheet has no left-facing sit or lie panel to trace, so a dedicated left trace would be an invented drawing; the mirrored unmarked silhouette stays and still NEEDS THE OWNER'S EXPLICIT ACCEPTANCE under the no-flip rule (the reviewers' static scan found no scale(-1) anywhere and no asymmetric element leaking).

decisions.sheet: The pose panels are drawn at different scales; their spot layouts are looser than the coat maps.
decisions.chosen: Sit and lie are scaled so their heads match the shared 3/4 head (eye spacing 46.4 units); check: the sit front leg (elbow to ground) is 179 units against 180 in the 3/4 view. Right-facing bodies carry the coat_right records placed on the posed parts (R-06, R-07 on the folded haunch; R-08 on the forearm) plus M-CHEST and L-09; the withers patch is traced from each panel (D16). Left-facing bodies carry the coat_left records placed at the matching anatomy, each a little further back along the body than its right-side neighbour, as coat_left draws them.
decisions.why: Size panel controls scale; coat maps control markings; pose drawings show the performance.

decisions.sheet: badger_pose_walking.png: one walking frame, far front paw landing well ahead of the chest, near hind leg extended back at toe-off, near fore planted under the chest, head carried up and forward, tail swept back.
decisions.chosen: REVISED in round 2: 4-beat lateral-sequence gait (duty 0.6, 375 units per cycle, stance sweep 225 units: fore lands 128 ahead and lifts 97 behind its shoulder, hind lands 96 ahead and lifts 129 behind its hip; shoulder glide capped at 26), lateral pairs close together so walkPhase 0 is the sheet frame (far fore landing, far hind just planted, near hind at toe-off, near fore in late stance). The round-1 stride (358.3, sweep 215) left the phase-0 paw spread about 10% short of the panel; the far fore of the right rig cannot reach further than 128 without the paw sliding, so the extra spread comes mostly from the hind. Paws are solved on their DRAWN outline: heel-up roll about the lowest toe point, a ground clamp keeps the traced sole on the ground line in stance and above it in swing, the swinging fore leg raises its scapula, the paw pitches toes-down at most 28 deg. Neck +2 deg, tail +34 deg while walking. Verified by dev/walkCheck.ts (see walk.verification).
decisions.why: v1.0.0 rolled the paw heel-down and pivoted on control points, pushing paws up to 22 units into the floor; its stride was short and the head low against the sheet frame.

decisions.sheet: Legs are single outlined shapes with no visible joint seams.
decisions.chosen: REVISED in round-1 repair: stroke-under-fill. Every exterior leg stroke (and the ring of any bent joint) is drawn at twice LINE.width first; the joint disks and segment fills go on top and hide every interior seam; interior creases (elbow lines) and toe details go last. The traced leg fills and strokes are inset by LINE.width / 2 (dev/trace/erode.py: only exterior edges move, cut corners slide along the cut), so the visible outline still covers the traced edge +- LINE.width / 2. The v1.0.0 occlusion masks are gone.
decisions.why: The masks left crumbs, spikes and stepped outlines at wrists and hocks in walk frames; this construction gives one continuous silhouette at any joint angle.

decisions.sheet: badger_pose_looking_up.png: right-facing, neck upright, head raised toward Zoo, pale near ear hanging back with its pink inner showing, one continuous throat line from the lip to the collar.
decisions.chosen: REVISED in round-1 repair: both look-up heads are their profiles pitched 40 deg (was 34) and joined to the rig necks in head-local space: the lip line ends at the commissure and ONE throat stroke lands on the neck's throat line (the lowest landing whose stroke passes in front of the old upper throat line, which a 6-unit coat band hides); the skull's back contour is stroked down past where it crosses the neck's back line (no nape gap). The hanging ear shows its inner at the fold (pale ear: front half; dark ear: a band). Right look-up mount: neck -12 deg (was -2), dx -7, dy +1.
decisions.why: Matches the panel's head carriage; removes the nape gaps, forked stubs and floating jaw the reviewers found.

decisions.sheet: badger_turn_34.png: the far contour runs OUTSIDE the far eye, the muzzle projects past the far cheek with the nose at its tip, the mouth is a long gently curved line under the nose, the far dark ear is solid, the chin is closed.
decisions.chosen: Superseded in round 2 by BADGER-D36 (the lower face, far contour and far ear of both 3/4 heads are re-authored from badger_turn_34.png). Round-1 text: one far contour from the far temple, pulled in at the far cheek, round the muzzle and the chin; near cheek stops at the jaw; far ear solid; irises 15% larger; lower-lip detail dropped.
decisions.why: Turnaround views control identity; the reviewers found the open chin and grin-like mouth on screen for 100 frames of the proof.

decisions.sheet: badger_coat_left.png: the patch spans 88 x 36 px below the top line, deepest in the middle, starting about 24 px behind the collar along the top line; the size panel (the default left view) shows it about 79 x 34 units with a clear gap behind the collar. coat_left's own top line over the patch lies about 5 px lower than the rig's, which is pinned to the binding withers height (312.6).
decisions.chosen: L-WITHERS (left) retraced: lower edge 5 px higher than the raw trace so its depth below the rig's top line matches coat_left (aspect about 2.3), front tip 7 px further back so the default left view keeps the size panel's gap behind the collar. Same id, same part.
decisions.why: Coat maps control the marking; the size panel controls the default view. The rendered v1.0.0 patch read as a deep half-disc touching the collar.

decisions.sheet: coat_left / coat_right profiles: a nose about 20 x 21 px (outer) set into the muzzle tip, a clear stop at the eye, a small dark almond eye, rose ears hanging from the top of the skull, one lip line running into the jaw.
decisions.chosen: Profile heads retraced (gen_heads.py): smaller rounded-wedge nose continuing the muzzle line, deeper stop, muzzle underside matched to each map, a profile eye drawn as a dark almond (iris colour, no white), a short commissure mark instead of a second lip stroke. The left (dark) ear outline already matched coat_left within about 1 px and is kept.
decisions.why: The reviewers measured the old profile nose 1.4x the sheet's and the eye about 2x; the doubled lip stroke read as a hook at the throat.

decisions.sheet: badger_expr_happy.png: a wide smile inside the face with raised corners, a notch at the philtrum and a lower-lip arc. badger_expr_shocked.png: a small open mouth (about nose width, 0.45 of the nose height) under a kept philtrum, jaw intact. badger_expr_worried.png: ear flaps lower and splayed. Eye lines are level on all four panels (measured tilt 0.0-0.6 deg).
decisions.chosen: Happy and shocked retraced from their panels (front and 3/4); shocked in profile and look-up heads is a closed, outlined open-mouth wedge inside the head silhouette. Worried / earsBack swings each front ear about 20 deg down and out without narrowing it. Judge lowers the lids at most to 0.86 open and folds the ears back slightly (eyes stay open between blinks); a closed eye is a nearly flat lid line. No default head tilt for happy or worried: the panels' eye lines are level, so tilt stays a composition choice.
decisions.why: Expression drawings show how the same character performs; the reviewers found happy indistinguishable from neutral and shocked twice the panel's size with the jaw open. Round-2 note on head angle: the happy, worried and shocked panels also turn the head about 15 deg to screen right; the front bust stays frontal and the turn is a staging choice made with the replacement heads (threeQuarterRightScreen carries all four expressions) plus headTilt, so one bust never mixes two head views.

decisions.sheet: No panel; CLAUDE.md records the owner's request that Badger's mouth and ears animate from real-dog sound clips through a mouth-open control, with no redesign.
decisions.chosen: Optional prop mouthOpen (0..1) on <Badger/>: each head view's own open-mouth drawing (the shocked mouth) grows down from the upper lip with the amount, the jaw line stays, and the ears lift slightly. Below 0.06 the expression's own mouth is shown. Nothing renamed.
decisions.why: Owner request; reuses the approved shapes only.

decisions.sheet: PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS call the collar plain slate (brand slate #161A21); the approved drawing renders it #393F45 (sampled), clearly lighter than the near-black outline.
decisions.chosen: BADGER_COLORS.collar = #393F45 with one shadow tone #2B3035 (palette.ts).
decisions.why: The drawing defines the asset (same reasoning as ZOO-C1 for the overshirt): #161A21 would merge with the near-black outline and lose the collar band at small scales.

decisions.sheet: The sheet draws a light silver split ring above the teal tag, and the front view's hind-leg strip between the front legs in coat white.
decisions.chosen: The tag ring is a closed loop filled BRAND.silver with a detail-width outline in every view; the front view's hind strip uses coat white.
decisions.why: The open U stroke read as two black ticks; the grey strip read as a shadow the turnaround does not draw.

decisions.sheet: The happy panel's inset carries the tail high in an upward curve; the art guide asks for breathing of a few px at proof scale.
decisions.chosen: With expression happy the side views carry the tail at least 32 deg above the stand (the wag stays restrained). Breathing scales the chest by 1.5% (was 0.6%), about 2 px at the proof scale.
decisions.why: Pose and expression drawings show the performance; the old breathing was sub-pixel.

decisions.sheet: badger_turn_front.png runs the forearm contours straight past the forearm spots and the hind strip's line into the inner contour of the leg in front of it; badger_pose_sitting.png and badger_pose_lying.png draw the back-of-neck line from under the ear to the collar (the cheek line branches off it), one neck-front line from the chin through the collar into the chest, the collar ending at the neck-front line, and (lying) one belly underline running to the foot of the elbow.
decisions.chosen: Traces repaired, nothing redrawn: front R-08 / L-09 contours straight past the spots (the spots stay inside the leg clip); the front hind strip line ends in the leg contour (no U-hook); sit / lie back-of-neck lines extended up under the ear with the neck fill closing the nape; lie throat joined to the chest line; sit chest line starts under the collar; collar front ends seated on the neck-front line (sit trimmed 4.5 px, lie extended 6.5 px, panel px); lie belly underline joined to the elbow line. The left-facing sit / lie reuse the same unmarked silhouette, so they carry the same repairs.
decisions.why: The reviewers found V-notches with spots bulging outside the front legs, a stepped hind strip, orphan neck strokes and open contours in the pose bodies.

decisions.sheet: badger_pose_walking.png and badger_turn_side.png outline every edge a moving part uncovers: the tail's underside down to the rump, the buttock behind a raised tail, the thigh's top and front when the leg swings, and soft concave curves on the inside of a bent hock or wrist.
decisions.chosen: Round 2 (gen_left.py, gen_right.py, erode.py, parts/Leg.tsx, parts/SideBody.tsx): the tail is one closed, fully stroked shape whose root stays inside the torso; the torso's rump runs on as a stroked buttock and flank fold where the thigh hides it at rest; the near thigh's top and back edges are stroked in an 'underlay' pass drawn under the torso, so only what a swing pushes outside the body shows; a bent wrist, hock or pastern gets a fillet tangent to both edges where they cross (radius 9 units); every leg fill carries a fill-coloured halo (0.3 x LINE.width) with the under-strokes widened to match, closing the anti-aliasing seams that showed as hairline ticks at the paws; short straight tracing nubs at segment cuts are no longer eroded as edges (they left ears outside the outline).
decisions.why: The round-2 review found unoutlined tail roots and rump / thigh wedges in every walk frame and the happy side views, a sharp kink at the far hock and hairline ticks at the front paws.

decisions.sheet: badger_turn_34.png (eyes aligned, 50 crop px = 46.4 units): the nose sits about 7 units beyond the far eye and 32 below the eye line, the far silhouette runs from under the far ear straight to the nose, a bridge line runs from below the far eye to the nose, the mouth rises to the far lip corner under the nose, the chin line is outlined about 15 units higher than the front head's, the far upper lip is shaded left of the philtrum, the far cheek spot is hidden by the muzzle, and the far dark ear is one solid shape.
decisions.chosen: Round 2 (gen_heads.py rebuild_three_quarter): the screen-right 3/4 head's skull outline, nose, bridge line, philtrum, four mouths, jaw and lip shadows and near cheek spot are re-authored on those measurements; the skull outline is one stroke over the top, round a rounded far-top corner behind the far ear, round the muzzle behind the nose and along the chin line; the far ear is one silhouette with one outline (the front-view inner and fold fills and strokes are gone). The screen-left head uses the same unmarked outline, nose and mouth geometry with x -> -x (as INT-B1 did); its ears, eyes and markings keep their own construction (pale far ear with its spot H-EAR-R-SPOT; near cheek spot H-CHEEK-L; far cheek spot hidden).
decisions.why: Turnaround views control identity. The reviewers found the nose under the far eye and 9 units low, a short muzzle, a white crescent in the far dark ear and a black needle and white nick at the far pale ear's root.

decisions.sheet: No panel shows a head turned back over the shoulder; on the left-facing body the 3/4-right head's far contour ran straight into the neck's back line beside the nose, so head and neck read as fused.
decisions.chosen: Round 2 (Badger.tsx LEFT_NAPE_34R / RIGHT_NAPE_34L, SideBody HeadMount.nape): when a side body carries the 3/4 head turned toward its back, the crest of the neck runs from behind the far ear past the muzzle (about 8-12 units clear) into the original back line above the collar, over a coat fill that hides the old line. Other head mounts are unchanged, so the proof's swaps keep their cranium positions.
decisions.why: The reviewers measured this as the proof's main Badger beat (about 3 s, f97-189).

decisions.sheet: badger_expr_neutral.png: the skull outline is continuous where the ears attach; the pale ear's pink band reaches its fold and bottom; the mouth is closed (gull-wing upper lip with the lower lip joined at the corners, about 33 sheet px either side of the philtrum); two nostril curls; no chin outline. badger_expr_worried.png: the flaps splay out and down (pale tip about 10 units out and 10 down, dark tip about 14 down at the worried amount).
decisions.chosen: Round 2 (gen_heads.py, parts/heads/Head.tsx): rounded skull corners under the ears and ONE skull outline from jaw to jaw, so folding an ear never opens it; the pale ear is one closed flap outline plus the band's free edge (no interior tick, no shelf stub, no white sliver); the dark ear's pale inner runs under the cap's hollow edge; the neutral mouth is the sheet's closed mouth; two nostril curls in line colour (no highlight tone); earsBack combines a smaller swing (pale -11.5, dark +20 deg at full) with a lengthwise stretch along the root-to-tip axis (pale 1.36, dark 1.21 at full; ear props stretch / axis).
decisions.why: Expression drawings show how the same character performs; the reviewers found an outline gap at the folded pale ear on the worried bust and the judge hold, a dangling jaw stub, a floating lower lip and worried ears that drooped instead of splaying.

decisions.sheet: badger_pose_looking_up.png: a long lip line inside the muzzle from just under the nose back over about 60% of the muzzle, parallel to the jaw's lower contour; a short diagonal cheek mark below the ear; one smooth throat line from the jaw angle to the collar.
decisions.chosen: Round 2 (gen_heads.py build_up): each look-up head draws the lip line 4.5 units inside the pitched jaw contour from 7% to 62% of its length (happy curls its end up, worried down; shocked keeps its open wedge), no commissure hook, a cheek mark placed from the eye as on the panel, and a throat that leaves the jaw along its chord and lands tangent to the neck's throat line (no S-curve). The throat still bows slightly forward where it meets the neck: the side rigs' neck front line sits forward of the raised jaw, so a fully concave throat needs a dedicated look-up neck pose.
decisions.why: The reviewers found no lip line, a cheek dash that read as a smile on the throat, a commissure hook and an S-shaped throat with a bump.

decisions.sheet: badger_size_comparison.png: Zoo screen left, Badger (left side toward camera, face turned to camera with a slight lean toward Zoo) screen right, one ground line.
decisions.chosen: Pair shots use one shared scale (both characters' world units are the same; 0.88 in the 1920x1080 proof), ground contact at 918 px (85% of 1080), Badger view 'left' with head 'front'. The proof opens with a +3 deg head tilt (muzzle toward Zoo) for the panel's lean; the 3/4-left head turns too far for it.
decisions.why: The size-comparison panel controls relative scale; same scale value = correct relative size.

decisions.sheet: The panel stands the pair 482.9 units apart (ground point to ground point); Badger's head sits just beside Zoo's hanging hand.
decisions.chosen: When Zoo points to screen right over Badger, the pair stands 560 units apart and Badger is drawn in front of Zoo (depth), for the whole shot (no sliding). Scale and ground line stay the panel's.
decisions.why: Re-measured on the repaired point path (ZOO-P2) in integration round 1: at the panel spacing the swinging hand overlaps Badger's pale ear at poseAmount ~0.2 (front and 3/4 heads), which reads as touching him. At 560 units the closest approach is 24.5 px at the proof scale (poseAmount ~0.26). Re-measured in integration round 2 on the round-2 arc (ZOO-P4 with POINT_OVERLAP) from Zoo-only and Badger-only renders of the proof: the fist passes 26.9 px (30.5 u) from the pale ear's tip at f96 on the way up and 30.9 px (35.1 u) at f188 on the way down, and Badger's eyes close as it passes (blinks f94-99 and f188-197), so the near miss reads as his reflex. A neck dip, head tilt or ear fold on Badger does not widen it (his neck pivots his head toward the hand); only a wider spacing would. Spacing is staging, not anatomy; relative scale is unchanged.

decisions.sheet: Prompt 2: proof is silent unless narration is supplied; mouth shapes are demonstrated separately.
decisions.chosen: Preview10s has no audio track; MouthDemo cycles the six shapes one per second with an on-screen note "Mouth library demo — silent, not lip-synced". Sheet stills render the rig with no labels copied from the model sheets. On-screen text says "Zoo" (owner amendment 2026-11-24).
decisions.why: PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS: do not claim lip-sync without an audio track; never use the labelled model sheet in scene.

decisions.sheet: zoo_pose_point.png shows the end pose only; Prompt 1 asks for restrained, purposeful gestures.
decisions.chosen: The point is timed along the hand's arc, not in poseAmount: gesture.ts maps a path fraction to poseAmount through the rig's own pivots and angle function (hand path 409 units). The swing eases the path fraction with bezier(0.38,0,0.4,1) over 16 frames (f90-106), ends past the hold pose and settles back ~1-2 deg (poseAmount 1 -> 0.993, f106-113), holds (decision INT-T2) and lowers along the same arc over 16 frames (f181-197).
decisions.why: The rig's joint path (round 2: monotone cubics through ARM_POINT_MID with POINT_OVERLAP timing) moves the hand 80% of its travel in the first half of poseAmount, so easing poseAmount directly snaps the swing (v1: 123 px in one frame). Arc-length timing peaks at ~45 px/frame at the proof scale (round 2, measured 44.5), like the lowering, and the hand-shape swaps (fist at 0.08, pointer at 0.4) land on fast frames (f95, f99).

decisions.sheet: zoo_pose_point.png shows only the end pose; Prompt 1 asks for restrained limited animation with purposeful gestures, and every hold must stay alive (the round-2 performance review: the hand moved 2 px or less over f106-181, so the gesture froze).
decisions.chosen: A moving hold, f113-181: the raised arm sinks from poseAmount 0.993 to 0.93 on one slow sine ease (shoulder 3.2 deg, wrist 2.8 deg; the elbow is unchanged near the end key), so the hand drops 9.2 px at the proof scale, 7.6 px with breathing included (measured on the rendered frames, ~0.15 px/frame mid-hold), and the lowering starts from that pose. Part-way through, Zoo nods once toward the point: a ~1.7 deg head tilt down and back (f124-142) with a blink that starts with it (f125). Badger answers after the nod with his small curious tilt (f140-180, was f132-180) and one blink (f158), so the two moves do not overlap.
decisions.why: The reviewer asked for ~0.05 poseAmount of drift (6-10 px at the hand) with a slow ease plus a 1-2 deg nod. On the round-2 arc the end key is carried by the shoulder, and the breathing cycle lifts the arms ~1.6 px over the same frames, so 0.063 gives a net 7.6 px; a deeper sink would read as the arm tiring. The head tilt is the rig's only head control, so the nod is a small tilt toward the point; the blink sells it as a nod.

decisions.sheet: The approved sheets draw no contact shadows (the size panel has only a ground line). ART_GUIDE CV4a/LS4: Badger's off-white coat (L* 4.9 from the background) and Zoo's sneakers (L* 0.4) separate from #E6E8EB only by their outline, so every shot showing feet or paws gets one flat contact shadow in backgroundShadow. The round-2 Badger review asked for it in the proof and the sheet stills.
decisions.chosen: BRAND.backgroundShadow #CFD3D8 (ART_GUIDE CV2; the value the branding, episode and show themes already use) is added to palette.ts as the background colour's one flat shadow tone. Preview10s, ZooSheet and BadgerSheet draw one flat ellipse under each figure (src/compositions/characters/contact.tsx, FOOTPRINTS: measured sole, paw, wheel or leg extents + 10 units, e.g. Zoo front rx 121, Badger 'left' rx 198; ry 15-16 units). In the proof the shadows sit over the silver ground line (the line passes behind the feet); on the sheets the near-black baseline runs over them, so it stays unbroken. No blur, opacity or gradient.
decisions.why: ART_GUIDE is the craft guide and PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS allows one flat shadow tone per colour; the background stays plain #E6E8EB. ART_GUIDE asks for the owner's sign-off on the palette entry, so it is recorded here and is still pending.

decisions.sheet: The sheet keeps a near-constant screen line weight: close-up panels (zoo_expr_*, badger_expr_*) draw outlines at about half of LINE.width in world units (1.4-2.1 units at 0.699 units/px).
decisions.chosen: Every composition passes lineScale to both rigs. Full-body framings use ART_GUIDE SL5 (outline clamp(3.5 x k, 3, 6) px, k = output px per unit): the proof pair at 0.88 gives 1.00, the Zoo sheet row at 0.54 gives 1.59, Badger's pose row at 0.5 gives 1.71. Close-ups keep the sheet's close-up weight (half of LINE.width), floored at 3 px and capped at 6 px: MouthDemo bust 0.50, sheet busts 0.74 (Zoo) and 0.60 (Badger).
decisions.why: Fixed world-unit strokes were about twice the sheet weight in close-ups and under SL5's 3 px floor on the small sheet rows.

decisions.sheet: Prompt 2: Badger looks toward the gesture with a small head turn, looks up at Zoo, then gives a restrained judging reaction. Prompt 1: emotion through brows, folded ears, head angle and tail; eyes open between natural blinks.
decisions.chosen: Every head replacement in the proof happens with Badger's eyes closed: the turn to the 3/4 head under a blink (f97), the look-up swaps (3/4 -> front breakdown -> upLeftScreen, f190/192) under a blink with the eyes and the neck leading, the neck values chosen so the cranium stays close across each swap (re-measured in round 2 with the re-authored 3/4 head, BADGER-D36/D37, and unchanged from round 1: the skull top rises 9 px at f97, in the direction of the rising neck that follows, and drops 7 px at f190 and 5 px at f192, each inside the closed-eye frames; a neckTurn or headTilt correction would trade it for a 10-15 px sideways jump). The judging look plays on the FRONT head (eyes kept on Zoo, judge brows, ears 0.42, ~8 deg tilt) after a slow blink covers the swap from the up head, with one slow push-in (1.00 -> 1.04, f196-299, ART_GUIDE MO13) anchored on his eyes. Idle life in 0-3 s: one blink and one ear flick.
decisions.why: The v1 look-up swapped three silhouettes in three frames with no blink (a pop and head-bob), and the judge on the pitched profile head moved each cue by only 2-7 px. On the front head each cue moves 6-8 px and the brows and lids read.

decisions.sheet: BADGER-D23 (revised): sit and lie exist in both facings.
decisions.chosen: BadgerSheet shows sit and lie in both facings (each pair faces each other so the left- and right-side markings sit side by side), plus walk and look-up, at scale 0.5.
decisions.why: The asset sheet should show every implemented pose body; the left-facing ones carry different markings (LEFT coat map).
